stories.title: US midterms: voters back data-centre bans, caps or restrictions in almost every local measure on the ballot (Data Centers on the Ballot tracker: restrict side won or leads in 51 of 59, allow side in 1; Hubbard, Ohio ban passed 2,622-802 per Trumbull County); Ohio had 21 of ~41 measures with at least 14 restrictions passing (Fortune); Texas and Georgia elect governors who campaigned for moratoriums; counts unofficial until certified

Ricursive Intelligence, which builds AI for chip design, releases Ripple-65B Preview: a dense 65B open-weight model (Apache 2.0) trained from scratch on 12T tokens, 1M context; claims US open-weight state of the art on TerminalBench 2.1 (80.52) above Reflection Beam 501B (80.1) and Meta Muse Spark Open 816B (76.4); full R&D cost $32M; on Hugging Face and OpenRouter ($0.20/$0.60 per M tokens)

Oracle has cancelled its ~$7B, five-year deal to lease about 100,000 advanced AI chips in Southeast Asian data centres to Tencent after US officials raised concerns, the FT reports (via Reuters, which could not verify it); Guangdong officials also urged Tencent to back domestic chips

Bloomberg: Chinese buyers including ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have ordered about $70B of Nvidia's export-legal RTX Pro 5500 (~$11,000 each, 84GB GDDR7) but will get only 'some tens of thousands, or roughly 1%' in the next few months; ~700,000 expected by end-2027; Nvidia criticises 'outdated' US export controls

Tencent releases the full Hy4 (770B total, 49B active, 1M context), adding computer use for the first time; claims gains over the August preview in long-horizon agentic work and game development; on OpenRouter (text and image in, ~$0.42/$1.25 per M tokens); weights and system card promised 'in coming days', Flash version soon

OpenAI agrees to buy Pierre Computer Company, maker of Code Storage (Git-based storage for agent-written code) and the Trees and Diffs libraries already used in Codex; terms undisclosed, libraries stay open source, needs regulatory approval

Meta acquires Conductor, an app for running several coding agents in parallel workspaces; the team joins Meta Superintelligence Labs; no new sign-ups, Conductor Cloud read-only 13 Nov and shut 20 Nov, local app supported until early 2027

MeitY launches three IndiaAI Mission models: Soket AI's EKA-1 (26B, 7.5T tokens, for air-gapped use in defence, cybersecurity and banking; weights promised within a month) and ZenteiQ's Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B, compact models that run offline on mobile phones

Apple cut some engineers' daily AI spending cap from $300 to $200 last month and plans cuts to as little as $100; some non-engineering teams could fall to $25 and some are told to use cheaper or on-device models (Bloomberg via TNW); Apple's R&D rose 32% in FY2026 on AI and infrastructure

Canva cuts 1,271 jobs (22% of staff) as growth slows for the first time in a decade; it had cut its 2026 revenue-growth forecast to 20% from 30% over ballooning AI costs and faces competition from ChatGPT and Gemini image tools

AMD reports record Q3 revenue of $13.4B (+45%) with data-centre revenue up 97% to $8.5B on EPYC and Instinct MI450; guides Q4 to ~$17B, which would put it ahead of Intel's guidance ($15-16B) for the first time
Qualcomm forecasts ~$650M of data-centre revenue in Q1 2027, $5B by the end of 2027 and $15B by 2029, about 30% of its business eventually, as smartphone sales fall ~20% (The Verge)
SemiAnalysis: SpaceX has raised its 2027 data-centre target to ~13GW, roughly all of Google's capacity built 1999-2026, with 3.6GW under construction and >9GW of sites identified by SemiAnalysis

Google will spend $15B in Malaysia in 2027-28 on data centres, cloud, water, power and training, expanding its Selangor campus and building new ones in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan, including a $160M water plant

UK AI minister Kanishka Narayan says the government's own estimate is that AI adds £55B-£140B (central £120B) by 2030, and that the £400B figure officials cited for two years came from a 2023 Google-commissioned Public First report (Wired)

Uber: in Halloween week, its busiest of October, about 320M trips and orders, of which four rides and about 500 Uber Eats orders were placed by AI agents; CEO: 'very, very early and very limited traction'

Check Point Research finds 'prompt adware': the Haiou jailbreak bundle for OpenAI Codex rewrites the agent's global instructions so greetings trigger adverts for an opaque OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway, and installs pentesting and cracking skills

Descope launches Envoy so consumer apps can accept personal AI agents with their own identity rather than the customer's password, built on the Personal Agent Protocol ('Poppy') 0.1 draft from Meta and Sierra

Pangram releases Pangram Image 1.0 (AI-image detection with heatmaps locating AI regions) and Image Flash 1.0 (AI-video detection); reports 99.96% accuracy on its own set of 1,200 synthetic mirrors of 100 real photos from 12 generators

On an Nvidia RTX Spark laptop, Linux locks the GPU at ~780MHz on wall power (vs ~2.2GHz on Windows) because the power table is encrypted and only a Windows component reads it: GPT-OSS-120B runs at 13.9 tokens/s on Linux vs 65.4 on Windows (MindStudio test; HN ~590 points)

Moonshot publishes Kimi K3.1 Pro's weights on Hugging Face as promised: ~2.78 trillion parameters, custom licence, natively multimodal agentic model post-trained from K3; replaces Gated MLA with Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention for long context; 1M context
stories.update: The weights are now public on Hugging Face (about 2.78T parameters, custom licence, ungated); the card adds the switch to Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention
